value.rationale: A complete regular-module multiplication Jordan spectrum is a natural invariant of a finite-dimensional local algebra. Four exterior generators is the first dimension where rank-two vs rank-four bivectors coexist, while arbitrary inhomogeneous multipliers introduce distinct degree-one wedge conditions; their exact interaction with characteristic leads to six or seven explicit arithmetic strata and a sharp collapse from length-three to exclusively length-two blocks. The whole distribution is more informative than generic linear-form ranks or a single finite-field sample and can be used for comparisons with modular group algebras and exterior-module invariants.
